title: Rigveda 3.44: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 3.44: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 3.44 is a hymn of 5 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 3, the family book of Viśvāmitra. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 229r-229v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 3.44.1-3 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 3, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 229r
translation.original_text:
1a̱yaṁ te̍ astu harya̱taḥ soma̱ ā hari̍bhiḥ su̱taḥ | ju̱ṣā̱ṇa i̍ndra̱ hari̍bhir na̱ ā ga̱hy ā ti̍ṣṭha̱ hari̍ta̱ṁ ratha̍m ||
2ha̱ryann u̱ṣasa̍m arcaya̱ḥ sūrya̍ṁ ha̱ryann a̍rocayaḥ | vi̱dvām̐ś ci̍ki̱tvān ha̍ryaśva vardhasa̱ indra̱ viśvā̍ a̱bhi śriya̍ḥ ||
3dyām indro̱ hari̍dhāyasam pṛthi̱vīṁ hari̍varpasam | adhā̍rayad dha̱rito̱r bhūri̱ bhoja̍na̱ṁ yayo̍r a̱ntar hari̱ś cara̍t ||
translation.text:
1May this delightsome Soma be expressed for thee by tawny stones. Joying thereat, O Indra, with thy Bay Steeds come:. ascend thy golden-coloured car.
2In love thou madest Ushas glow, in love thou madest Sûrya shine. Thou, Indra, knowing, thinking, Lord of Tawny Steeds, above all glories waxest great.
3The heaven with streams of golden hue, earth with her tints of green and gold- The golden Pair yield Indra plenteous nourishment: between them moves the golden One.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 229r (numbered 39r by the scribe) (OPenn image 230, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 3.43.6 ‹-yujānāḥ arvāk indra sadha-mādaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 229v (numbered 39v by the scribe), begins in RV 3.44.4 ‹-vṛṣā viśvam ā bhāti›. Verses 3.44.1-3 end on this page.

2haryan | uṣasam | arcayaḥ | sūryam | haryan | arocayaḥ | vidvān | cikitvān | hari-aśva | vardhase | indra | viśvā | abhi | śriyaḥ

translation.original_ref: RV 3.44.4-5 (aṣṭaka 3, adhyāya 3, varga 8); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 229v
translation.original_text:
4ja̱jñā̱no hari̍to̱ vṛṣā̱ viśva̱m ā bhā̍ti roca̱nam | harya̍śvo̱ hari̍taṁ dhatta̱ āyu̍dha̱m ā vajra̍m bā̱hvor hari̍m ||
5indro̍ ha̱ryanta̱m arju̍na̱ṁ vajra̍ṁ śu̱krair a̱bhīvṛ̍tam | apā̍vṛṇo̱d dhari̍bhi̱r adri̍bhiḥ su̱tam ud gā hari̍bhir ājata ||
translation.text:
4When born to life the golden Bull illumines all the realm of light. He takes his golden weapon, Lord of Tawny Steeds, the golden thunder in his arms.
5The bright, the well-loved thunderbolt, girt with the bright, Indra disclosed, Disclosed the Soma juice pressed out by tawny stones, with tawny steeds drave forth the kine.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 229v (numbered 39v by the scribe) (OPenn image 231, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 3.44.4 ‹-vṛṣā viśvam ā bhāti›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 230r (numbered 40r by the scribe), begins in RV 3.45.4 ‹na prati-jānate vṛkṣam pakvam›. Verses 3.44.4-5 end on this page; 3.44.4 begins on fol. 229r (numbered 39r by the scribe).
